counterfactual_missing_items: No central scar or microcystic pattern (would favor serous cystadenoma)
decisive_items: cystic lesion in the uncinate process with a smooth-walled capsule containing calcifications, enhancing septa, millimetric nodules, and soft-tissue components
complex cystic mass in the pancreatic head measuring 5.5 × 4.5 cm with internal calcifications and mural nodularity
complex cystic mass in the pancreatic head
response.rationale: The uncinate-process cystic lesion with enhancing septa, millimetric nodules, and soft-tissue components in an asymptomatic 63-year-old woman is most consistent with branch-duct IPMN with high-risk stigmata. MCN is less likely because it typically arises in the body/tail of younger women; SPN is atypical at this age; serous cystadenoma lacks mural nodules/solid components; pancreatic cancer is usually solid and would more often show metastases or duct obstruction.

rejected.why: Serous cystadenoma is unlikely because mural nodularity, enhancing septa, and soft-tissue components are not typical; calcifications alone are nonspecific.
SPN is atypical in a 63-year-old; the uncinate location and enhancing septa/nodules favor IPMN.
Pancreatic cancer is usually a solid mass; this is a smooth-walled cystic lesion without metastases or lymphadenopathy, and breast cancer history is nonspecific.
